decision.rationale: The claim is for 38.00 EUR for dinner in Amsterdam on 2026-10-14. It is rechargeable under client code ORL-0391. The itemised receipt (Café de Klos, ref KLOS-381, 20:30) totals 38.00 EUR and matches the claim, which meets EXP-1.2. The items are ribs, fries and 2 colas. None is listed as alcohol. compare_to_history lists one unusual item: the merchant has never been seen before. The category z-score is 2.0 and the employee z-score is 2.6. Neither is above 3, so I don't call them unusual. There are no repeats. The topic check predicted Equipment at 0.51 confidence and did not match the Meals category. I can't resolve this from the data I have. The policy has two routes for a meal, and I can't tell which one applies. (1) EXP-2.1 allows a late working meal of up to £20 per person for staff working past 8pm at the office or a client site. The email doesn't say Sofia was working late or where. I also have no GBP conversion for 38.00 EUR, so I can't compare it with the £20 cap. CHG-1.2 says rechargeable claims have the same limits. (2) PD-1.1 and PD-1.2 allow a per diem of 55 EUR for Amsterdam on overnight business travel, instead of individual receipts. The claim doesn't say whether the travel was overnight. A human needs to confirm the business context (late working, location, overnight travel) and the EUR to GBP rate. They then need to decide whether to cap the claim at £20, treat it as a per diem, or reject it.
